title: Threat modeling
summary: Map untrusted inputs to the side effects they can reach, and name the deterministic boundary, authenticating principal and audit evidence for each mutation.

provenance.notes: Reduces ECC's hardening guidance to one question per mutation: who is authenticated, what enforces the limit in code, what is recorded, and what happens on failure.

inputs.name: change
inputs.description: The feature or diff to model.

inputs.name: assets
inputs.description: What an attacker would want: data, credentials, execution, approvals.

outputs.name: threat-table
outputs.description: Per mutation: input source, principal, enforcing code, audit record, failure behavior.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Missing or prompt-only controls, by severity.

workflow.step: List every source of untrusted data: request bodies, repository files, tool output, model output, environment, files from other users.
workflow.check: Model output and repository text are on the list.

workflow.step: List every side effect: file writes, process execution, network calls, database writes, approvals, deployments.
workflow.check: Each effect is a function you located.

workflow.step: For each (input, effect) pair identify the authenticated principal and the code that enforces the limit. A rule that exists only in a prompt is not a control.
Ask what happens on malformed input, missing context, timeout and partial failure; the answer must be deny.
Check what is recorded for audit and whether the record can be rewritten by the actor it describes.
workflow.check: Audit data is append-only or signed.

workflow.step: Propose a negative test for each high-risk row.

constraints: Report weaknesses and defenses; do not produce working exploit code.
Do not treat a hash as proof of authorship; ask who could have recomputed it.
Advisory only: a threat model never grants approval.

examples.title: Caller-asserted identity
examples.situation: A review function trusts a verifierId string passed by the caller.
examples.guidance: Flag it: any caller can claim the trusted identity. Require a signature checked against a runtime-owned keyring.

verification: Every mutation row has an enforcing function and a deny-on-failure statement.
Each critical row has a proposed negative test.

task.text: Threat model this feature: trust boundary, attack surface and untrusted input to side effects.
Design with abuse case analysis of privilege and attacker capabilities.
Review the spelling in the docs.
